limitations.title: Community-bank capital reporting
limitations.text: Since 2020 many small banks use the community bank leverage ratio and report no risk-based ratio. v5 relies on the leverage ratio instead. These banks score less well (ROC-AUC 0.830 against 0.864; top-10% capture 47.8% against 56.4%) because training ends before the framework began.

limitations.title: The largest banks
limitations.text: For banks over $100bn the model is weak (ROC-AUC 0.666), and most of their distress cases come from the two-losses rule or the 2023 failures. Not reliable for those banks.

limitations.title: Slight over-prediction
limitations.text: Probabilities run a little high (35% predicted against 29-30% observed in the riskiest tenth). The bands are set from observed rates, so their meaning holds; read a probability as a ranking more than an exact chance.

limitations.title: Small losses at tiny banks
limitations.text: Two losses in a row count as distress however small. Transact Bank, CO ($6.5m of assets) lost $3,000 in 2026 Q2 (FDIC call report), and that counts.

limitations.title: Securities losses
limitations.text: Net income includes realised gains and losses on securities, so a one-off bond sale reads like weak earnings.

limitations.title: Young and merged banks
limitations.text: Banks just past the three-year cut-off can still have start-up economics, and a merger changes growth, capital and earnings in one quarter.

limitations.title: Credit risk and earnings risk share one list
limitations.text: Banks just under the 3% non-current-loan line (32 of the top 50 in 2026 Q2) and banks with thin earnings both rank high; the reasons show which kind of risk a bank carries.

limitations.title: Assistance counted as failure
limitations.text: The failure part of the label uses every row of the FDIC failure list, which also holds assistance transactions such as the January 2009 open-bank assistance to Bank of America's banks.

limitations.title: Public data only
limitations.text: Quarterly call reports, about two months after quarter-end. No supervisory ratings, examinations or deposit-level data. A screening tool, not a rating.

next.text: Count losses only when they are material; separate securities gains and losses from operating earnings; treat young and recently merged banks with care; report credit risk and failure risk separately; a 'what if' re-score with a group of measures set to the median.
